title: German scientists explore whether solar power plants can induce rain in deserts
summary: The research project combines LiDAR measurements with advanced meteorological simulations to assess the climatic impacts of large-scale photovoltaic installations in desert regions.

title: Brazil deploys 4.4 GW of solar in Q1
summary: Brazil added 4.4 GW of solar capacity in Q1 2026, led by 2.3 GW of utility-scale and 2.2 GW of distributed generation, with continued strong expansion expected if current rates persist.

title: Heterojunction PV modules with low silver content tested in world’s sunniest region
summary: Chilean company Atamostec is testing low-silver heterojunction solar modules under real desert conditions at the Atacama Desert Solar Platform (PSDA) in partnership with France’s CEA-Ines. The ALPACA project has so far achieved up to 70% silver substitution with copper.

title: Fraunhofer ISE achieves 31.3% record solar-to-hydrogen efficiency in photovoltaic electrolysis
summary: Researchers at the German institute built a photovoltaic water electrolysis system based on micro-concentrator photovoltaics coupled to proton exchange membrane electrolysis. Outdoor testing demonstrated a record solar-to-hydrogen efficiency of 31.3%, achieved by a four-junction CPV system driving two PEM cells in series under real operating conditions.

title: Chinese PV Industry Brief: Daqo, Tongwei, Aiko Solar post Q1 losses
summary: Chinese solar manufacturers reported sharply mixed Q1 results amid ongoing polysilicon and module price pressure, with output increases, weak demand-driven margin compression, and continued net losses.

title: China TOPCon module prices hold steady as supplier price gap widens
summary: In a new weekly update for pv magazine, OPIS, a Dow Jones company, provides a quick look at the main price trends in the global PV industry.

title: HY Solar unveils 670 W TOPCon modules with 24.8% efficiency
summary: HY Solar has launched the HT3.0 quad-cut module at its Jiangyin base, marking an upgrade to its n-type portfolio built on TOPCon 3.0 cell technology with up to 27.5% cell efficiency. The manufacturer said the new product features PSP quad-cut architecture, high bifaciality and low degradation.

title: Mitsubishi launches propane air-to-water heat pumps for large homes, light commercial applications
summary: Mitsubishi has expanded its Hydrolution EZY R290 heat pump series with two models with capacities of 10 kW and 14 kW. The new products use R290 refrigerant and can deliver up to 75 C flow temperatures.

title: Inox Clean buys U.S. PV manufacturing assets of Boviet Solar for $750 million
summary: Through this million asset purchase, Inox Clean acquires 3 GW of operational TOPCon solar module manufacturing capacity in the United States, aligning with the “Make in America, For America” initiative.

title: India installs 15.3 GW of solar capacity in Q1
summary: India installed 15.3 GW of solar capacity in the first quarter of 2026 – the highest quarterly addition on record – representing a 143% year-on-year increase, according to Mercom India.

title: France’s collective solar self-consumption model hits regulatory wall
summary: A roundtable recently held by solar panel manufacturer Dualsun and the GoodPlanet Foundation in Paris highlighted the organizational and regulatory barriers holding back collective solar self-consumption in France, a model its proponents say is technically ready to scale.

title: Solar industry faces rising risks from fires and battery faults
summary: The 8th annual Solar Risk Assessment from kWh Analytics identifies equipment-driven fires, regulator fines, and battery inaccuracies as the latest threats to renewable asset returns.

title: Sweden lacks national strategy for utility-scale solar
summary: Research from Lund University has explored how Sweden is building out utility-scale solar in the absence of an overarching national strategy. The researchers told pv magazine that without clearer national direction, projects will cluster in areas with favorable conditions while stalling elsewhere.

title: German storage industry back on growth path, says BVES
summary: After a significant decline in 2024, revenues for energy storage companies based in Germany grew substantially last year and are expected to rise further this year, according to market analysis from BVES. However, industry uncertainty continues to rise.

title: From night to noon: France’s reactors are now bending for European solar
summary: Hourly ENTSO-E data show the summer midday-to-evening gap in French nuclear output has grown nearly eightfold since 2019. The reactors have adapted. The rest of the European power system has some catching up to do.

title: Solomon Islands plans first large-scale solar project
summary: The Solomon Islands Electricity Authority and Asian Development Bank have signed an agreement aimed at developing the country’s first large-scale solar project.

title: Grid-forming tech on centre stage as search for system resilience steps up
summary: Maintaining grid stability becomes more challenging as the share of intermittent renewables grows in the electricity generation mix, but system resilience is essential to continued solar deployment. Grid-forming inverters offer a solution, and their capabilities are increasingly being tested and relied upon in key energy markets globally.

title: Bruges appoints independent solar broker offering free advice
summary: The city of Bruges is offering small- to medium-sized enterprises and organizations looking to install large-scale rooftop solar free advice from an independent solar broker. The solar broker will be available to support the entire installation process, from initial calculations through to final commissioning.

title: Genex cuts Bulli Creek solar to 300 MW, adds 1.7 GWh storage
summary: Genex has announced plans to reconfigure the first stage of its 2.5 GW Bulli Creek multi-stage development in Australia from a 775 MW solar farm to 300 MW, adding a 425 MW / 1,700 MWh battery energy storage system (BESS).

title: AI model uses cloud type and cover to predict solar power swings
summary: A machine learning model uses cloud type and cloud cover to predict rapid changes in surface solar irradiance, including short-term “ramp” events that affect grid stability. When tested across 15 global sites, it showed strong generalizability, with most locations matching or exceeding the original model’s predictive performance, though extreme climates performed less consistently.

title: The EPA is expediting clean air permits for power plants to remove ‘unnecessary delays’
summary: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency is expediting Clean Air Act permit reviews to eliminate delays, allowing concurrent public comment and review.

title: Elective pay explained as key IRS deadline approaches | Q&A with tax credit specialist Bryen Alperin
summary: Municipalities, schools, and first-time applicants are accelerating projects under the IRS's elective pay provision before the May 15 deadline.

title: Amazon turns to geothermal, solar and storage to power Nevada data center growth
summary: The 700 MW portfolio includes Zanskar’s 20-year agreement to deliver 100 MW of baseload geothermal power to NV Energy by 2030.

title: Should data centers pay for grid upgrades? Oregon regulators think so
summary: The Oregon Public Utilities Commission approved Portland General Electric's proposals for charging data centers for infrastructure costs.

title: What’s driving the evolution of the utility industry? | Top takeaways from IEEE PES 2026
summary: IEEE PES 2026 showcased an evolution in utility thinking that’s needed to ensure grid reliability and customer affordability in both the short and long term.

title: SEIA names former Minnesota Governor new president and CEO
summary: The Solar Energy Industries Association named former Minnesota Governor Tim Pawlenty president and CEO, effective June 15.

title: More spill, less hydropower: The electric grid tradeoffs Washington can’t ignore
summary: Every megawatt of hydropower lost, whether to dam removal or spill, must be replaced by something else at a time the region is already facing shortages, writes Washington State Standard's Kurt Miller.

title: California, Nevada and Arizona announce temporary plan to save water from the Colorado River
summary: Arizona, California, and Nevada plan to cut Colorado River water use by up to 1 million acre-feet through 2028 to support reservoirs amid drought.

title: How S&C is embedding distributed intelligence to support grid resilience and reliability
summary: Jeremiah Karpowicz goes behind-the-scenes at S&C Electric Company, a more than 100-year-old Chicago-based manufacturer, to lay eyes on a bevy of distribution-level electric power solutions.

title: Those damn data centers | Factor This Brief
summary: Data center sentiment is nosediving. Meanwhile, Moment Energy raises money for repurposed EV batteries, California approves a hybrid solar-plus-storage project under a new permitting program, Xcel Energy gets approval for a new gas peaker plant, CMBlu Energy hits unicorn status, and ESS Tech commissions two iron-flow energy storage systems.
